- **Output dir follows the worktree.** `DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR` was a constant computed from `__file__`, which always pointed at the main checkout's `docs/conversations`. Replaced with `default_output_dir()` returning `<first project root>/docs/conversations`. From a worktree this writes the conversation file alongside the journal entry, so a single commit on the worktree branch captures both.
- **Why `--git-common-dir` parent.** `--show-toplevel` from a worktree returns the worktree path, not the main checkout. `--git-common-dir` returns `/path/to/main/.git` for both worktrees and the main checkout (the shared `.git`); its parent is the main checkout root. Deduped against the worktree root, this gives `[worktree, main]` from a worktree and `[main]` from the main checkout. Falls back to `[cwd]` when not in a git repo.

## 2026-05-15 21:11 - [Bugfix] Fix 314k-token context blowout from Merge ProxyProvider, redesign aggregator around progressive disclosure

**Conversation:** [2026-05-15-2111-2447523d.md](conversations/2026-05-15-2111-2447523d.md)

Hermes WebUI was showing **157% context used / 314.4k tokens** on the user's first message after redeploy — over the 200k Claude window before they typed a character. Root cause: `template_repos/hermes_agent/doh_runtime/mcp_aggregator.py:161-163` unconditionally attached a Merge `ProxyProvider` at boot, transparently re-exporting the entire 151-connector Tool Pack (~1500 tool defs averaging ~200 tokens of schema each) into Hermes's `tools/list`. The fix replaces the transparent passthrough with a progressive-disclosure surface — four always-on tools the LLM uses to discover, inspect, and invoke arbitrary integration tools.

**Diagnosis path.** Confirmed it was *us* (not upstream) by reading the deployed image's `tools/list` flow against the 314k figure. The number had to be **tool definitions**, not chat history (first message), and Hermes vanilla doesn't ship anywhere near that. Found the unconditional `_attach_provider(slug="merge")` line and traced it to `MergeBackend.list_tools` → ~1500 namespaced tools.

**Design grilled in `grill-me`.** Long, useful interview that nailed seven decisions before any code:
1. **Aggregator stays in-container, alpha-style** (engine, not shim). Notion's `_OAuthState` and per-user state already live there; splitting state across DOH/container would be worse. Per-(app, user) is *practically* per-app since each Hermes app has one owner.
2. **DOH stays stateless on catalog**. No DOH-side cache; aggregator pulls fresh from `/api/integrations/merge/mcp` through the existing relay on boot, and via a user-facing **Refresh button** in the Integrations panel header (rate-limited 30s) when needed.
3. **Catalog in-memory only.** Persistence buys ~1-3s of boot savings vs a real engineering tax (atomic writes, schema migration, "is this stale because…"). Container restarts are infrequent enough that the cost is tiny. Restart = re-fetch.
4. **BM25 search, not embeddings.** Pure-Python `rank_bm25` (~50 LOC, zero deps). LLM is already great at query rewriting; semantic embeddings are a v2 problem. Indexed text per entry: `tool_id + connector + description`.
5. **Mutation classification: verb-prefix heuristic + static `*_MUTATION_OVERRIDES` dict per backend, default-to-mutates on ambiguity.** Asymmetric cost — over-prompting for approvals is worse than silent mutations. Different verb tables for Merge's `connector__verb_object` and Notion's `verb-object-thing`.
6. **Tool ids = native upstream names verbatim.** Considered DOH-namespacing (`connector.action`) and aggressively bounced it during grilling — overdesign. Native names mean no normalization layer, no mapping table, no rename-handling complexity. Backends stamp `connector` and `mutates` as metadata fields on `CatalogEntry`. If two backends ever advertise the same name, log loud, last-write-wins.
7. **The 4 primitives**: `integrations_search_tools(query, limit, status_filter)`, `integrations_describe_tool(tool_id)`, `integrations_call_tool(tool_id, args)`, `integrations_list_connectors(status_filter)`. Naming went through `merge.search` → `search_tools` → namespaced `integrations_search_tools` (because Hermes already exposes terminal/file/web/etc. and bare names collide). Settled on uniform `integrations_*_*` shape so the four read as a coherent set in tool listings.

**Pre-flight verification of fastmcp's API.** Instead of dropping to JSON-RPC for `tools/list`/`tools/call`, confirmed `fastmcp.Client.list_tools()` and `Client.call_tool()` exist at `~/.cache/uv/.../fastmcp/client/mixins/tools.py:62, 191`. Saved a chunk of code.

**The `Backend` Protocol.** Each backend implements `list_catalog`, `list_known_connectors`, `call`, `connector_status`, `invalidate_caches`. **MergeBackend** uses the existing DOH-side relay (`/api/integrations/merge/mcp` for tools, `/api/integrations/merge/connectors` for the connector roster, `/api/integrations/merge/connector-status` for per-connector state). **NotionBackend** uses the existing `_OAuthState` + Notion's hosted MCP (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`) directly. Both reuse the WebUI-facing OAuth + Merge passthrough Starlette routes — those weren't deleted, just freed from being on the LLM-facing path.

**Three rounds of in-container verification on `hermes-vmendi01`** revealed three real issues, each fixed:

1. **Initial deploy: bloat fixed but 7 connectors only.** `tools/list` returned exactly 4 tools to Hermes (definitive: 314k → ~few k tokens), search/describe/call worked. But `integrations_list_connectors` showed only 7 connectors instead of the expected 151. Diagnosed: my `MergeBackend.list_catalog` derived `connector` from `name.split("__", 1)[0]`, which left `authenticate_<slug>` placeholders Merge ships for unconnected connectors falling into a `connector="unknown"` bucket. They also had inflated BM25 scores because their description packs every downstream tool's docs (a Merge quirk). **Fix: skip `authenticate_*` entirely; they're meta tools the LLM has no reason to call (connection happens via Magic Link UI, not a tool call) and they pollute search.**

2. **Second deploy: 7 connectors still, but reason is structural.** Merge only exposes *action* tools after the user OAuth-authenticates. Unconnected connectors literally don't appear in `tools/list` (just the auth-tool placeholder we now skip). So `list_connectors` derived from the catalog can never surface unconnected ones. **Fix: split the catalog into two indexes — `entries: dict[tool_id, CatalogEntry]` for callable tools, and `connectors: dict[(backend, slug), _ConnectorIndex]` populated from a new `Backend.list_known_connectors()` method.** MergeBackend's implementation hits the existing `/api/integrations/merge/connectors` endpoint (which returns all 151 from the Tool Pack with their `status`). Search now returns mixed results: `kind=tool` for callable tools, `kind=connector` for known-but-unconnected connectors with a hint to open the Integrations panel.

3. **Third deploy: 152 connectors, but `list_connectors` showed asymmetry between OAuth and public-API connectors.** When the user asked the LLM "what mcp tools do you see," it correctly listed Jira (43 tools, connected) but bucketed Weather/Wikipedia/etc. (which are public-API, no auth required) as "not connected with tools available when connected" — confusing because their tools are *immediately* callable. Root cause: Merge marks a connector as `authenticated` only after an OAuth grant; for no-auth public APIs, status is permanently `not_connected` even though the tools work. **Fix: in `CatalogStore._reload_locked`, after folding tool counts into the connector index, promote `status` to `connected` when `tool_count > 0`** — `connected` now means "callable right now," consistently across OAuth and public-API connectors. Also added a `_connector_status_for_entry()` helper so per-tool calls/searches consult the catalog index (which factors in tool_count) rather than calling `backend.connector_status` directly, avoiding the same OAuth-only signal mismatch in `integrations_call_tool`.

**Final shape on `hermes-vmendi01`** after all three deploys:
- `tools/list` returns exactly **4 tools** to Hermes.
- Catalog: **97 callable tool entries, 152 connectors** from 2 backends, 0 collisions.
- `connected` = "callable now" (Jira via OAuth + 6 public-API connectors with no auth).
- `not_connected` = ~145 OAuth-gated connectors awaiting Magic Link.
- Search returns `kind=connector` shells for queries like "slack" / "send email", correctly pointing the LLM at the Integrations panel.

**SOUL.md additions** — three workflow rules so the LLM uses these primitives correctly without per-call reminders: "search before invoking" / "on `not_connected` tell user to open Integrations panel" / "if `mutates: true` confirm before calling."

**Refresh button.** New `POST /__doh_broker/integrations/refresh_catalog` endpoint on the broker's Starlette app, plus a button in the Integrations page header. Drops both catalog and per-backend connection-status caches, rebuilds the BM25 index. Rate-limited (30s server-side, JS inflight flag client-side).

**Async catalog load with `asyncio.Event` gate.** `serve()` kicks `asyncio.create_task(catalog_store.load_in_background(...))` and starts FastMCP immediately — sandbox `/mcp` comes up unblocked. Each of the 4 tools `await store.ensure_loaded(timeout=30)` first thing; first call waits for catalog if not yet loaded, subsequent calls are no-ops. Lenient partial backend failure: per-backend `gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` style, a failed backend contributes zero entries, others keep working.

**Lessons:**
- **The tool-pack relay was a footgun.** Transparent passthrough seemed clean but mixed two responsibilities: "let DOH manage the API key" (the actual goal) and "expose every Tool Pack tool to the LLM" (an unintended side effect). Splitting these via a stateful aggregator with explicit primitives is better. The DOH-side relay still exists and still owns the API key boundary; just the *aggregator's* role changed.
- **Merge's catalog API has no `read_only`/`mutates` flag.** Tried to find one in their docs — public docs are thin (mostly 404s on the API reference URLs). The naming convention (`connector__verb_object`) is the only signal. Heuristic + per-tool overrides is the right shape until we discover a flag.
- **`connected` should mean "callable," not "credentialed."** The Merge API conflates the two; we need the looser, callability-based definition for the LLM to give coherent answers.
- **Don't await catalog load in `serve()`.** Tested briefly: a slow Merge response stalls container startup, and ECS health checks start failing. Async kick + per-call gate is strictly better.
- **The grill-me skill produced ~30% better design than my first instinct.** Several of my early proposals (DOH-namespaced tool IDs, search-engine in DOH, embeddings-first search, 4 primitives + connect URL surfacing) got bounced as overdesign during grilling. Worth using on any non-trivial system change.

## 2026-05-15 19:37 - [UI] Promote Integrations to a top-level page in the Hermes WebUI

**Conversation:** [2026-05-15-1937-89d09b66.md](conversations/2026-05-15-1937-89d09b66.md)

Moved the Integrations entry out of the Settings overlay and made it a primary navigation destination in `template_repos/hermes_agent/webui-extension/{doh.js,doh.css}`. Clicking the rail icon now replaces the chat in the center column with a connectors page, while the sidebar shows a small "Integrations" header + an "X of Y connected" summary. Verified end-to-end on `hermes-vmendi00` after a series of redeploys against CH Sandbox.

**The path-finding problem: where does the entry live?** Started by adding a `.nav-tab` to `.sidebar-nav` (matching the local clone of hermes-webui at `/Users/vmendi/agents/hermes-webui`). Looked correct in source, deployed cleanly — but invisible in the browser. Root cause: the deployed Hermes WebUI is **0.51.63**, which introduced a new `<nav class="rail">` icon strip and gates the legacy `.sidebar-nav` to mobile only (`@media(min-width:641px){.rail{display:flex;}.sidebar > .sidebar-nav{display:none;}}`). My local clone was older. **Lesson: when editing a webui-extension that runs against a pinned upstream, source the DOM contract from the deployed container (`curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/`), not from a local working copy that may have drifted.** Fix was to register a button in BOTH the rail and the sidebar-nav (mobile fallback) — defensive in case upstream evolves further.

**Treat Integrations as a `main-view`, not a `panel-view`.** Hermes 0.51 has a documented main-view switching contract: each top-level destination is a `<section class="main-view" id="main<Name>">` sibling of `#mainChat` inside `<main>`, plus a CSS rule `main.main.showing-<name> > #main<Name>{display:flex}`. The wrapper around `switchPanel` toggles `showing-<name>` on `<main>`. Originally I rendered the integrations content as a sidebar `panel-view` — wrong abstraction; it produced a vertical drawer next to the chat. Once we restructured as `#mainIntegrations.main-view`, the page took the full center column. Had to add `main.main.showing-integrations > #mainChat { display: none !important; }` because upstream's default-show rule (`main.main:not(.showing-...)... > #mainChat { display:flex; }`) hard-codes the list of known states and `:not(.showing-integrations)` isn't in there — without `!important` we'd be force-overriding upstream by patching CSS.

**Sidebar UX iterations.** First: hid the sidebar entirely while integrations is active (`:has(> main.main.showing-integrations) > .sidebar { display: none }`). User noticed clicking conversations in *other* panels then went weird because the rail's "second click collapses the sidebar" toggle interacted with our hiding. Then: tried showing the chat sessions list in the sidebar while integrations is the main view (manually re-activating `#panelChat` after `switchPanel` ran). User then noticed clicking a session didn't navigate (because main was stuck in `showing-integrations`). Final shape: own `panel-view#panelIntegrations` with a `.panel-head` title and a "X of Y connected" summary, leaving upstream's switchPanel behavior untouched. **Lesson: don't fight upstream's component contracts. Build your panel-view; let switchPanel manage activation; don't reach in.**

**`fromRailClick: true` on `switchPanel` is non-negotiable for rail buttons.** Without it, the rail icon wouldn't toggle the sidebar collapse on second click, breaking parity with every other top-level entry. Initially dropped it (during the sidebar-hiding experiment) and the rail UX felt subtly wrong in a way that took a beat to articulate.

**Performance: the slow first paint isn't the DOM, it's the `/__doh_broker/integrations` round-trip.** ~150 cards rendered all-at-once after a multi-second blank period. First reflex was `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` on logo `<img>` — done, but barely moves the needle since lazy-load only kicks in after the broker responds. Real fix shipped: prefetch from `init()`. The extension script loads `defer`, runs after DOM parse but before `DOMContentLoaded`, so firing `refreshAndRender()` from `init()` starts the broker request as soon as the page lands. By the time the user clicks Integrations, `_current` is usually populated and rendering is instant. Cost: one extra request per session; the chat panel's first paint is unaffected because `fetch()` is non-blocking. This also populates the sidebar summary up front, so the count is visible without ever opening the page.

**Logo background: chased the wrong dragon.** Some Merge logos (Basecamp, bioRxiv, Box) are dark-on-light and disappeared against our dark theme. Tried successively: subtle white-alpha (default; too dim), `#fff` (too harsh), `#808080` (universally ugly, midtone makes both light and dark logos look bad), `#f5f5f5` (still felt out of place against the dark page), `rgba(255,255,255,0.7)` (let the bg bleed through — interesting but the warm-gray didn't read as a "tile"). Settled on pure `#fff`. **Lesson learned the hard way: there is no single tile color that flatters all 150 vendor logos. Pure white is what Merge.dev itself uses on their dark-themed catalog — accept the aesthetic cost in exchange for guaranteed legibility.** A future user-research-grade fix would be #4 from our brainstorm (canvas-sample corner pixels, apply tile only to dark/transparent logos) or #7 (drop logos entirely, render colored circles with first-letter avatars).

**Verification cadence.** Every change required a full `doh_control redeploy-app` round-trip (~5min build/push/deploy via the job worker) on `hermes-vmendi00`. The customer-debug skill's `doh_app_exec --container hermes` was the workhorse for confirming each redeploy actually shipped the new file (`grep ensureSidebarTabAndPane /opt/doh/webui-extension/doh.js`) and that the in-container WebUI was serving it (`curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/extensions/doh.js`). The container has TWO copies of the extension files (`/opt/doh/webui-extension/` and `/hermes-persistent-root/opt/doh/webui-extension/`) — both update on redeploy, but worth knowing if you ever need to hot-patch from the host.

## 2026-05-15 01:50 - [Integrations] Merge.dev Agent Handler integration — ~150 connectors via DOH-relayed MCP

**Conversation:** [2026-05-15-0153-2a813baf.md](conversations/2026-05-15-0153-2a813baf.md)

Added Merge.dev's Agent Handler product as a third "kind" of integration in Hermes, alongside Google (TLS-intercept) and Notion (direct OAuth). Merge brokers OAuth for ~150 SaaS connectors (Slack, GitHub, Linear, Asana, Shopify, …) behind a single MCP endpoint — one DOH-tenant API key authenticates DOH to Merge, per-end-user identity is scoped via "Registered Users" in the URL path. End-user OAuth credentials live entirely in Merge's storage; we never touch them. Final shape: 196 unique tools surfaced through `sandbox → aggregator (loopback) → DOH (env bearer relay) → ah-api.merge.dev`, verified end-to-end on a freshly-deployed `hermes-vmendi01` in CH Sandbox.

**The hard architectural decision: where does the Merge API key live?** The naive answer — inject it into the broker sidecar like any other integration secret — would be a serious cross-tenant break. Merge's API key authorizes operations across **every** Registered User in the DOH-Merge tenant; if a customer admin reads `/proc/<broker_pid>/environ` (which they trivially can with `ecs:ExecuteCommand`, this is the standard ECS threat model), they exfiltrate a credential that lets them impersonate every other DOH customer's apps by enumerating `origin_user_id` strings (which are deterministically derivable from public-ish state). The Google integration already taught us this lesson — Google's OAuth `client_secret` lives only on DOH's control plane, the broker only ever holds short-lived per-user access tokens. Merge has to mirror that pattern. The cost is a runtime DOH dependency for Merge tool calls (DOH down → Merge tools fail) and one extra internet hop on the hot path. Acceptable; same shape as Google's refresh dependency, just at finer granularity.

**Identity = `f"doh_{user.pk}_{app_slug}"` is per-app, not per-user.** Multiple agents owned by the same DOH user can have entirely separate Merge connections. The user's intuition pushed this — "two different hermes agents, even if they belong to the same user, could have different integrations" — and it cleanly solves the destroy/recreate semantics: same-user-recreate-same-slug carries integrations over (familiar redeploy story); different-user-takes-over-the-slug starts fresh (OAuth grants don't leak to a new owner). Verified that `App.slug` is unique per organization (not globally — `UniqueConstraint(organization, slug)`), so the `user.pk` prefix is what prevents cross-tenant collisions when two orgs both have an app called `support-bot`.

**No DB column on DOH for `registered_user_id`.** Merge's create-or-409-with-existing-UUID path makes per-call resolution cheap (~one round-trip per cold worker). The DOH endpoints derive `origin_user_id` from authenticated state on every call and let Merge's own `non_field_errors` regex parsing return the existing UUID. We trade DB persistence (more state, migrations, eviction logic on app destroy) for slightly more chatty Merge calls, which is the right call at our scale.

**Six narrow DOH endpoints, not one generic proxy.** `ensure-registered-user`, `link-token`, `connectors`, `connector-status`, `disconnect`, `mcp` (streaming relay). Each one is a least-privilege gate: the URL path components (`tool_pack_id`, `registered_user_id`) are constructed server-side from authenticated state, never from caller input. The user pushed back on this initially — correctly noting that within an org, a single `/merge/proxy` endpoint with bearer-derived identity validation gives the same security as six narrow endpoints. The argument that survives the pushback is cross-org isolation plus forward-compat: with six narrow endpoints, adding a new Merge operation requires an explicit DOH change. With a generic proxy, future Merge endpoints (including ones with new URL shapes or body-scoped identity) auto-leak. Engineering taste, not security gospel.

**Sandbox identity reaches DOH via headers, not URL.** The MCP relay endpoint can't read `app_slug`/`owner_username` from the body — that's the JSON-RPC payload, opaque to us. Initially passed identity in query string, but the FastMCP `Client` doesn't expose query-param hooks cleanly. Switched to `X-Doh-App-Slug` and `X-Doh-Owner-Username` headers attached at the aggregator's `client_factory`. `_resolve_caller` reads headers first, falls back to query/body for the simpler endpoints. Clean; no body manipulation; works for both shapes.

**Magic Link flow uses no `callback_url`.** Each customer's Hermes container lives at `<app-slug>.<their-hosted-zone>` — every customer brings their own ALB hosted zone. There's no DOH-wide pattern Merge could pre-allow-list, and per-customer registration at deploy time would be a new failure mode in the deploy path. Without `callback_url`, Merge's hosted page shows a generic "authentication complete" message and the user closes the tab manually. WebUI compensates with a two-stage modal — explainer first (which mints the token only on Continue, preserving the 30-min single-use window), then a waiting modal that polls `connector-status?slug=<slug>` every 3s with a 5-min cap. The narrow per-connector status endpoint (vs. fetching the full 151-connector catalog every poll) keeps the load bounded; the user vetoed the more elaborate hygiene I had drafted (caps + backoff + visibility-change pauses) once the narrower endpoint made it cheap.

**Reauth follows Path α (agent relays the magic link in chat).** When a Slack token expires mid-conversation, Merge returns an `authenticate_meta` payload inside the MCP tool response with a fresh `magic_link_url` and a `message` field "written for the model to relay verbatim." We don't intercept or rewrite this — the response flows through the relay untouched, the agent surfaces it in chat, the user clicks. No DOH or broker special-casing. The alternative (Path β, intercept-and-surface in WebUI) would have been intrusive and fragile if Merge's response shape changes.

**Five surprises uncovered against the live API.** The Merge documentation page describing the `link-token` endpoint had bad shape information; verifying against `ah-api.merge.dev` directly was load-bearing. (1) `POST /registered-users/` is NOT idempotent — duplicates return HTTP 400 with the existing UUID embedded in `non_field_errors`. We parse the UUID via regex and treat the call as successful. (2) Response field for create is `id`, not `registered_user_id`. (3) Per-user connection state is not a separate endpoint; it's an `authenticated_connectors` array on the Registered User record itself (`GET /registered-users/{id}/`). (4) Link-token field is `connector` (not `connector_slug`); endpoint path needs trailing slash; success status is 201. (5) Disconnect is `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/registered-users/{rid}/connectors/{slug}/` — not on the Registered User record itself. Lesson: when integrating with a third-party API, probe the live endpoint before writing the client. Docs lie; live responses don't.

**The FastMCP `Client(headers=)` trap, again.** First implementation passed `headers={...}` to `Client()` — same kwarg-mismatch bug that bit the Notion integration two days earlier (see 2026-05-14 entry). Symptom is identical: `tools/list` silently returns `[]` because `ProxyProvider._list_tools` swallows the `TypeError` from the factory. Fix: use `StreamableHttpTransport(url=..., headers=...)` explicitly and pass it to `Client()`, which accepts a transport positional. Should have remembered this — but the journal entry from the prior session called it out, so the cost was just one redeploy.

**The precursor refactor was worth doing first.** Before adding Merge, I split a separate PR (`e894b2b`) that consolidated all browser-facing integration management under `/__doh_broker/*`. Previously Notion's OAuth lived under `/__mcp_aggregator/*` and Google's controls under `/__doh_broker/*`, which conflated "MCP transport" with "integration management." Merge would have inherited the same wart. Cleaning up first meant PR2 was purely additive on a clean foundation — no new URL conventions, no extra reverse-proxy patches. The user's instinct was right that mounting the OAuth handlers from `MCPAggregator` onto the broker's Starlette router is the right ownership split: aggregator owns provider state and the methods that mutate it; broker owns routing and the unified status endpoint. `MCPAggregator.routes(prefix=...)` factors this — the aggregator declares its own URL surface, the broker splats the routes into its router.

**One global Tool Pack today; per-org later.** Cross-tenant security comes from per-app `origin_user_id`, not from per-tenant Tool Packs. A customer CIO who wants to disable a connector for compliance reasons can't do it today; when that need arrives, we add a `merge_tool_pack_id` column on `Organization` and provision per-org packs. URL construction is already server-side, so the migration is mechanical. YAGNI'd it explicitly.

**End-to-end verification, three layers:** (1) DOH-side endpoints exercised against real Merge with the test API key, all six endpoints returning expected shapes. (2) Local Django integration test (`test_integrations_broker.py`) updated for the Starlette-based control app via `starlette.testclient`; 15/15 tests pass. (3) Full deploy of `hermes-vmendi01` to CH Sandbox via `doh_control deploy-app-template`, broker logs showing `attached provider merge (kind=doh_relay)` and `merge ensure-registered-user OK at boot`, `tools/list` through the sandbox-loopback aggregator returning **196 unique tools** flowing across all three hops. The redeploy step caught the `Client(headers=)` bug because the local test wasn't deep enough to exercise the upstream MCP factory — the lesson there is that any integration that puts a third-party MCP behind FastMCP's `ProxyProvider` should be deploy-tested at least once before being declared done.

**Key points:**
- The single most important architectural decision was rejecting the "inject Merge API key into the broker" shape. The hierarchy is: tenant-wide secrets stay on DOH (Google `client_secret`, Merge API key); per-user/short-lived tokens may transit to the customer container; nothing else crosses the boundary. Future integrations should fit this same hierarchy or come with a strong argument for why they don't.
- `origin_user_id = f"doh_{user.pk}_{app_slug}"` is the load-bearing identity formula. It's per-app (so different agents owned by the same user have separate connections), per-tenant-via-`user.pk` (no cross-org slug collisions), and survives same-user destroy/recreate (preserves connection state). Renames being disallowed at the App level is what makes this stable.
- Verify against the live API before writing the client. Five gotchas in our case: non-idempotent create, `id` not `registered_user_id`, `authenticated_connectors` on the user record (no separate endpoint), `connector` not `connector_slug`, disconnect path under `/credentials/`. The docs page implied otherwise on every one of these. The OpenAPI spec at `https://docs.merge.dev/openapi.yaml?api=3dccaac7-ad6b-4cf0-a548-7d7f19b5a1ce` is the authoritative source — and even there I had to verify `link-token` field naming by sending three variants until one worked.
- FastMCP's `Client()` doesn't accept `headers=`. It's the second time this bug hit. The fix is `StreamableHttpTransport(url=..., headers=...)` then `Client(transport)`. Cost both times: one wasted deploy. Worth a Hermes-side wrapper to enforce the right calling convention if we add a third FastMCP-relay provider.
- Two PRs in sequence (refactor first, additive second) was the right shape. The user's "let's clean up the mess first" was the call that made the Merge work pure-additive. Tempting to bundle, but the diff review story is much cleaner separated.
- The Merge API key on DOH means hot-path DOH dependency for Merge tool calls. Acceptable cost — same shape Google already accepts for token refresh — but worth flagging on a status page if/when DOH outages start mattering for customer-facing reliability.
